transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I'm here because I've been feeling constantly down and depressed for a really long time now. It's been going on for over two years, and I just can't seem to shake this heavy sadness.

During these past two years, have you experienced any periods of two months or longer where you felt completely free of these symptoms, or has the sadness been present almost every day without a break?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all. This sadness and depressed feeling have been with me almost constantly for the past two years and a month. I don't think I've gone even a few weeks, let alone two months, feeling completely back to normal.
Besides the constant sadness, have you been experiencing other issues like changes in your appetite, sleep patterns, energy levels, or trouble concentrating?

My sleep has been really disrupted—I have trouble falling asleep, wake up constantly, have nightmares, and never feel rested even if I sleep for a long time. As for my appetite, energy levels, or concentration, I'm not really sure and haven't noticed anything specific.
During this time, have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, or do you find it hard to feel any enjoyment at all?

Yes, I find it really difficult to feel any enjoyment at all anymore. I have this constant sense of inner emptiness, and my emotions feel completely dulled and numb. It's like I can't experience pleasure in anything these days.
Have you experienced any feelings of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or thoughts that life is not worth living during these past two years?
No, I haven't really experienced feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt. I also haven't had any thoughts of ending my life or felt like it wasn't worth living.

Looking back to when this all started two years ago, did these feelings of sadness and emptiness come on gradually over time, or was there a specific event or period where you noticed a sudden shift in your mood?
I'm really not sure, to be honest. I can't recall any specific event or trigger that started all of this. It just feels like it gradually crept up on me over time.
